ui_schema_slice.description: Stream UNet/DiT blocks between CPU and GPU so only a few stay resident.
ui_schema_slice.help: SDXL, Cosmos Predict2, Krea 2 and Qwen-Image 2.1; requires pipeline_stages = 1. Works for both adapter and full-model training: adapters keep their small trainable params resident, while full-model (no [adapter]) additionally requires optimizer.gradient_release so the per-parameter step runs while the block is on the GPU. On ~8 GB cards this is the lever that makes a full SDXL fine-tune fit (e.g. blocks_to_swap = 6 → ~4.3 GB). Combine with activation_checkpointing. With gradient_release set, the Block-swap prefetch toggle appears. Qwen-Image 2.1 on 8 GB: blocks_to_swap = 24 with the fp8 base (transformer_fp8_matmul). See the low-VRAM recipe in the doc.
ui_schema_slice.label: Blocks to swap

ui_schema_slice.description: Speed up block-swap transfers: pinned-DMA copies always, plus compute overlap when VRAM allows.
ui_schema_slice.help:
One switch, two effects (the offloader applies whichever fits — you don't tune them separately):
• Pinning (always, on CUDA): page-locks the swapped weights' CPU memory so each H2D copy runs as a full-bandwidth DMA instead of a ~half-speed pageable copy. This costs host RAM (the locked weights, a few GB), NOT VRAM, so it helps at ANY blocks_to_swap — including maximal swap, where it roughly halves step time on its own.
• Overlap (only when blocks_to_swap leaves ≥2 blocks resident): also prefetches the next block on a side stream while the current one computes. This keeps a second block resident, so it costs +1 block of VRAM and engages only when there is headroom for it.
Works for both adapter (LoRA/LoKr — streams only the frozen base weights, keeps the trainable adapters resident) and full-model (gradient_release) runs; loss is identical. Recommended ON whenever you block-swap and have spare host RAM. Turn it OFF if host RAM is tight (pinning can't page out), and note that on a nearly-full GPU the overlap's extra resident block can tip you into sysmem paging — measure the per-step cuda_peak_gb.
ui_schema_slice.label: Block-swap prefetch (overlap)

ui_schema_slice.description: Steps between empty_cache() calls while block swap is active (default 10).
ui_schema_slice.help: The single-buffered swap path allocates many shape-varying tensors per step, fragmenting the reserved pool by hundreds of MB between reclaims; a 50-step cadence let it grow 0.3-0.8 GB. Set 0 to disable, or raise it if the reclaim itself shows up in your step time. Lower it if a tight blocks_to_swap OOMs only after many steps.
ui_schema_slice.label: Block-swap cache reclaim interval

ui_schema_slice.description: Load the full backbone onto GPU for eval passes even when blocks_to_swap is on.
ui_schema_slice.help: Gives more accurate eval loss at the cost of temporarily using full-model VRAM. Enable if eval results look wrong with block swap active.
ui_schema_slice.label: Disable block swap for eval

ui_schema_slice.description: Each entry becomes one item under preview.prompts in TOML.

ui_schema_slice.label: Enabled

ui_schema_slice.description: Generate preview images every N optimizer steps.
ui_schema_slice.help: Lower values give more frequent quality checks at the cost of extra inference time per step. Combine with preview_before_first_step for a baseline.
ui_schema_slice.label: Preview every N steps

ui_schema_slice.description: Generate preview images at the end of every N epochs.
ui_schema_slice.help: Alternative to preview_every_n_steps for epoch-based runs. Preview inference runs after the epoch save, so it does not delay checkpointing.
ui_schema_slice.label: Preview every N epochs

ui_schema_slice.description: Run one preview pass before step 1 to capture the untrained baseline.
ui_schema_slice.help: Useful for visually comparing the model's output before and after training begins.
ui_schema_slice.label: Preview before first step

ui_schema_slice.description: Load the full backbone onto GPU for preview sampling even when blocks_to_swap is on.
ui_schema_slice.help: Faster previews at the cost of temporarily using full-model VRAM. Enable if preview quality looks degraded with block swap active.
ui_schema_slice.label: Disable block swap for preview

ui_schema_slice.description: Negative prompt applied to every preview image (SDXL).
ui_schema_slice.help: Shared across all preview prompts. Leave empty for Cosmos/Anima, which does not use a negative prompt during sampling.
ui_schema_slice.label: Negative prompt

ui_schema_slice.description: Preview image width in pixels.
ui_schema_slice.help: Set to a resolution your model supports; mismatch with the trained resolution can make previews look blurry or distorted.
ui_schema_slice.label: Width

ui_schema_slice.description: Preview image height in pixels.
ui_schema_slice.help: Set to a resolution your model supports; mismatch with the trained resolution can make previews look blurry or distorted.
ui_schema_slice.label: Height

ui_schema_slice.help: Only used by preview prompts with control_images: each condition image keeps its aspect and is resized to an area of control_resolution² (floored to 32 px), like training control images. Empty uses the side of the preview width × height (1024 by default). At least 256 (the vision encoder's minimum area).
ui_schema_slice.label: Edit preview condition resolution

ui_schema_slice.description: Denoising steps per preview image (Qwen-Image 2.1 default 28).
ui_schema_slice.help: Euler steps over the reference sigma schedule (resolution-aware shift, last step at 0.02). The reference sampler uses 40; 28 keeps previews faster.
ui_schema_slice.label: Inference steps

ui_schema_slice.description: Base RNG seed for preview images.
ui_schema_slice.help: Fixed seed produces consistent previews across steps so changes in quality are clearly visible. Change if the seed happens to pick an unrepresentative starting noise.

ui_schema_slice.description: Optional seed offset applied per training step.
ui_schema_slice.help: The default 0 keeps each prompt's noise fixed across steps so previews show model evolution. Set a positive value only when you intentionally want different noise at every preview.

ui_schema_slice.help: Enable if preview sampling OOMs; the transfer adds latency but lets the DiT use more VRAM during generation.

ui_schema_slice.help: Reduces preview VRAM at the cost of slower sampling. Raise if preview sampling OOMs after enabling preview_offload_text_encoder. Qwen-Image 2.1 on 8 GB cards: 32 (all blocks).

Uncheck to train all weights (full finetune); also set optimizer.gradient_release = true and blocks_to_swap if the full model does not fit in VRAM.
adapter:_has_adapter.label: Train with adapter (LoRA / LoKr / LyCORIS)

adapter:adapter.block_size.description: DyLoRA: the rank trains in nested blocks of this size; rank must divide evenly (default 4).
adapter:adapter.block_size.help: Each step updates a random sub-rank that is a multiple of block_size, so the exported LoRA stays usable when truncated to any multiple of block_size after training. Smaller blocks give finer rank choices but noisier updates.
adapter:adapter.block_size.label: Block size

adapter:adapter.constraint.description: OFT: caps the rotation magnitude per layer; 0 = uncapped (default).
adapter:adapter.constraint.help: Positive values bound the norm of the rotation generator (scaled by layer width) — the constrained-OFT variant. Raise it from 0 if the adapter drifts the model too far from base behavior. Exported as the file's per-module alpha.
adapter:adapter.constraint.label: OFT constraint

adapter:adapter.decompose_both.description: LoKr: decompose both Kronecker factors (default false).
adapter:adapter.decompose_both.help: LoKr only. When true, both Kronecker factors are low-rank decomposed instead of just one — more expressive but larger. Default false. Leave off unless you specifically need the extra capacity.
adapter:adapter.decompose_both.label: LoKr decompose_both

adapter:adapter.dora_wd.description: DoRA weight decomposition on top of this algorithm: the adapter trains the direction, a per-channel magnitude trains separately (default off).
adapter:adapter.dora_wd.help: Splits each adapted weight into a trained magnitude (dora_scale) and the algorithm's delta as direction. Often tracks full finetuning better at low rank, at a per-step compute cost. Toggle it on locon/loha/lokr to add DoRA to that base.
adapter:adapter.dora_wd.label: DoRA decomposition

adapter:adapter.dropout.description: Probability of dropping adapter activations during training (default 0.0 = off).
adapter:adapter.dropout.help: Probability of dropping adapter activations during training, in [0, 1]. Default 0.0 (off). Small values (e.g. 0.05–0.1) can regularize and reduce overfitting on small datasets. Applies to LoRA and all LyCORIS types.
adapter:adapter.dropout.label: Dropout

adapter:adapter.dtype.help: Precision the adapter (LoRA/LoKr) weights are stored and updated in; forward matmuls still run in model.dtype via autocast. In bfloat16 a plain-optimizer update below ~0.2% of a weight's magnitude rounds to zero, so training can stall (flat loss, normal grad norm) — keep float32 unless you pair 16-bit with a Kahan/stochastic-rounding optimizer (adamw8bitkahan, adamw_optimi). A kaon optimizer (adakaon, nekaon, …) instead handles this through its own bf16_method kwarg: "stochastic_rounding" (default, no extra state), "kahan8"/"kahan16" (compact Kahan, for low LR or fp32 fidelity), "kahan" (legacy, fp16 only), or "none". See the optimizer guide.
adapter:adapter.dtype.label: Adapter dtype

adapter:adapter.factor.description: Shapes the LoKr Kronecker split per layer; -1 (default) picks the most balanced pair.
adapter:adapter.factor.help: -1 splits each dimension into near-square factors (128 -> 8x16, 512 -> 16x32). A positive value forces that factor when it divides the dimension (factor 4: 128 -> 4x32) — smaller factors shrink the adapter at some capacity cost. Leave at -1 unless you are matching a known recipe or chasing a smaller file.
adapter:adapter.factor.label: LoKr factor

adapter:adapter.full_matrix.description: LoKr: use full matrices for the second factor (default false).
adapter:adapter.full_matrix.help: LoKr only. When true, the second Kronecker factor uses full matrices instead of a low-rank approximation — higher capacity at the cost of size. Default false.
adapter:adapter.full_matrix.label: LoKr full_matrix

adapter:adapter.init_from_existing.description: Start from an existing LoRA/LoKr (.safetensors or folder).
adapter:adapter.init_from_existing.help: Path to a prior run export or downloaded adapter. Folder should contain adapter_model.safetensors (or a single .safetensors file).
adapter:adapter.init_from_existing.label: Init from existing adapter path

adapter:adapter.layer_groups.description: Train the adapter only on these layer groups (pick one or several). Empty trains every targeted linear. Combines with the include/exclude glob patterns below.
adapter:adapter.layer_groups.help: Train the adapter only on these layer groups (pick one or several). Empty trains every targeted linear. Combines with the include/exclude glob patterns below.
adapter:adapter.layer_groups.label: Layer groups

adapter:adapter.module_dropout.description: Skips the entire adapter on a layer with this probability per step (default 0.0 = off).
adapter:adapter.module_dropout.help: Each step, an adapted layer keeps base-only behavior with this probability, so the frozen model stays visible during training. Use a small value if the adapter drowns out the base model's general knowledge.
adapter:adapter.module_dropout.label: Module dropout

adapter:adapter.rank.description: Controls how many parameters the adapter adds (typical values: 8, 16, 32).
adapter:adapter.rank.help: Higher rank = more adapter parameters and larger saved file. Alpha defaults to rank (scale 1.0); raise alpha for stronger adapter effect, lower for weaker. If results look blurry or under-trained, try a higher rank; if the adapter overrides the base too aggressively, lower rank or alpha.
adapter:adapter.rank.label: Rank

adapter:adapter.rank_dropout.description: Zeroes random rank rows of the adapter each step (default 0.0 = off).
adapter:adapter.rank_dropout.help: Per-step dropout over the adapter's rank dimension, in [0, 1]. A light value (0.05-0.1) regularizes inside the low-rank factorization; try it if a small dataset overfits before the style converges.
adapter:adapter.rank_dropout.label: Rank dropout

adapter:adapter.rescaled.description: OFT: adds a trained per-channel scale on top of the rotation (default off).
adapter:adapter.rescaled.help: Pure OFT only rotates weights, preserving their norms. Rescaled OFT adds a learned diagonal scale (saved as 'rescale'), letting magnitudes change too — slightly more expressive, slightly less base-preserving.
adapter:adapter.rescaled.label: Rescaled OFT

adapter:adapter.rs_lora.description: Scales the adapter delta by alpha/sqrt(rank) instead of alpha/rank (default off).
adapter:adapter.rs_lora.help: Rank-stabilized LoRA: standard scaling shrinks the effective update as rank grows; sqrt scaling keeps it steady. Worth trying at rank 32+. The exported per-module alpha is adjusted (alpha x sqrt(rank)) so loaders reproduce the trained strength unchanged.
adapter:adapter.rs_lora.label: Rank-stabilized scale

adapter:adapter.target_exclude.description: fnmatch globs removed from the include set (applied after includes).
adapter:adapter.target_exclude.help: Same path matching as Target include. E.g. *ff* (SDXL) or *mlp* (Cosmos) leaves the feed-forward layers untrained. If include and exclude together match nothing, the run fails at startup instead of training an empty adapter.
adapter:adapter.target_exclude.label: Target exclude patterns

adapter:adapter.target_exclude~963a2a.description: Skips modules whose path matches any of these glob patterns, applied after the include list (empty = skip none).
adapter:adapter.target_exclude~963a2a.help: Same path matching as Target include. E.g. *ff* (SDXL) or *mlp* (Cosmos) leaves the feed-forward layers untrained. If include and exclude together match nothing, the run fails at startup instead of training an empty adapter.
adapter:adapter.target_exclude~963a2a.label: Target exclude patterns

adapter:adapter.target_include.description: fnmatch globs over dotted module paths; only matching linears get the adapter. Empty = all. Layer groups above expand into these patterns.
adapter:adapter.target_include.help: Patterns match the full dotted module path (e.g. unet.down_blocks.0...attn1.to_q on SDXL, blocks.0.self_attn... on Cosmos). *attn* trains attention only — smaller file with the capacity focused on composition/identity instead of textures.
adapter:adapter.target_include.label: Target include patterns

adapter:adapter.target_include~92278a.description: Only attaches the adapter to modules whose path matches one of these glob patterns (empty = all modules).
adapter:adapter.target_include~92278a.help: Patterns match the full dotted module path (e.g. unet.down_blocks.0...attn1.to_q on SDXL, blocks.0.self_attn... on Cosmos). *attn* trains attention only — smaller file with the capacity focused on composition/identity instead of textures.
adapter:adapter.target_include~92278a.label: Target include patterns

adapter:adapter.type.description: Options depend on the selected model.
adapter:adapter.type.help: LoRA exports the widely compatible lora.safetensors; LoKr and every LyCORIS type export adapter_model.safetensors with kohya-style keys (loads in ComfyUI). LyCORIS types use the lycoris-lora library: LoCon (classic LoRA), LoHa (Hadamard product), LoKr (Kronecker product), DoRA (LoCon + weight decomposition, often closer to full finetune at low rank), DyLoRA (trains nested ranks so you can truncate after training), GLoRA (adds input-side adaptation), Diag-OFT and BOFT (orthogonal rotations that preserve base-model weight norms).
adapter:adapter.type.label: Adapter / network type

adapter:adapter.unbalanced_factorization.description: LoKr: swaps which output factor each Kronecker side gets (default off).
adapter:adapter.unbalanced_factorization.help: The output dimension factors into a (small, large) pair; this gives W1 the large one instead. Capacity moves between the two Kronecker factors — a recipe-matching knob, leave off otherwise.
adapter:adapter.unbalanced_factorization.label: Unbalanced factorization

adapter:adapter.use_scalar.description: Adds a trained scale that starts at 0 so the weight factors can init non-zero (default off).
adapter:adapter.use_scalar.help: Standard init zeroes the up factor so training starts as a no-op; use_scalar instead initializes both factors and multiplies the delta by a learned scalar starting at 0. The scalar is folded into the exported tensors, so files stay loader-compatible.
adapter:adapter.use_scalar.label: Trained scalar

adapter:adapter.wd_on_output.description: Computes the DoRA magnitude over the output axis (default on).
adapter:adapter.wd_on_output.help: Only matters when DoRA decomposition is active (dora_wd). On = one magnitude per output channel (lycoris default); off = per input column. Leave on unless reproducing a recipe that used the input axis.
adapter:adapter.wd_on_output.label: DoRA output axis

checkpoint:async_model_export.description: Overlaps the model export's disk write with training: the CPU snapshot still happens synchronously, but the safetensors write runs on a background thread so the next training step doesn't wait on I/O. Auto-disabled (falls back to synchronous export) when pipeline_stages > 1.
checkpoint:async_model_export.help: The CPU state-dict snapshot still happens synchronously (so training resumes safely), but the safetensors write to disk runs in the background — the next training step starts immediately instead of waiting on export I/O. Off by default. Auto-disabled (falls back to synchronous export, with a warning) when pipeline_stages > 1.
checkpoint:async_model_export.label: Async model export

checkpoint:checkpoint_every_n_epochs.description: Write a DeepSpeed resume checkpoint at the end of every N epochs.
checkpoint:checkpoint_every_n_epochs.help: Stores full optimizer and scheduler state for training resumption; not a usable inference file. Combine with max_checkpoints_to_keep to limit disk use.
checkpoint:checkpoint_every_n_epochs.label: Checkpoint every N epochs

checkpoint:checkpoint_every_n_minutes.description: Write a DeepSpeed resume checkpoint after this many wall-clock minutes.
checkpoint:checkpoint_every_n_minutes.help: Use on long runs to limit the distance back to the last safe resume point if training crashes.
checkpoint:checkpoint_every_n_minutes.label: Checkpoint every N minutes

checkpoint:keep_exports_from_step.description: Drop scheduled exports below this training step before applying max_model_exports_to_keep.
checkpoint:keep_exports_from_step.help: Drop scheduled exports below this training step before applying max_model_exports_to_keep.
checkpoint:keep_exports_from_step.label: Keep exports from step

checkpoint:max_checkpoints_to_keep.description: Limit DeepSpeed global_step* folders kept on disk.
checkpoint:max_checkpoints_to_keep.help: Oldest checkpoints are pruned; latest always points to the newest.
checkpoint:max_checkpoints_to_keep.label: Max checkpoints to keep

checkpoint:max_model_exports_to_keep.description: Cap scheduled export folders (step*/epoch*); signal_step* exports are never auto-deleted.
checkpoint:max_model_exports_to_keep.help: Works together with keep_exports_from_step when both are set.
checkpoint:max_model_exports_to_keep.label: Max model exports to keep

checkpoint:save_dtype.description: Dtype for exported adapter or full-model weights.
checkpoint:save_dtype.help: Same keys as model dtype (bfloat16, float16, float32). Applied when writing save folders.
checkpoint:save_dtype.label: Save dtype

checkpoint:save_every_n_epochs.description: Export adapter or full-model weights every N epochs (default 1).
checkpoint:save_every_n_epochs.help: Writes an epoch1/, epoch2/, ... folder usable in ComfyUI/Forge. Reduce to save fewer intermediate files; increase max_model_exports_to_keep if you want them all kept.
checkpoint:save_every_n_epochs.label: Save model every N epochs

checkpoint:save_every_n_examples.description: Export model weights every N training examples (converted to steps using global batch size).
checkpoint:save_every_n_examples.help: Alternative to save_every_n_steps when you want to compare runs with different batch sizes at the same data exposure.
checkpoint:save_every_n_examples.label: Save every N examples

checkpoint:save_every_n_steps.description: Export model weights every N optimizer steps.
checkpoint:save_every_n_steps.help: Writes folders like step500 under the run directory. Can be combined with save_every_n_epochs.
checkpoint:save_every_n_steps.label: Save model every N steps

compile:compile.description: torch.compile on the DeepSpeed pipeline model (recommended for long runs).
compile:compile.help: Applies torch.compile to the whole pipeline model (UNet/DiT). Cosmos/Anima (≥1000 steps): after warmup, steady steps were ~0.51s vs ~0.68–0.70s without compile. Early steps are slower while Inductor/CUDA graphs build; short test runs are not representative. Tune behavior with compile_mode and compile_dynamic below.
compile:compile.label: torch.compile

compile:compile_cache_dir.description: Where the on-disk compile cache lives (must be ext4/255-char). Default: a 'compile' subdir of the dataset cache_root.
compile:compile_cache_dir.help: Directory for compile_disk_cache. Defaults to <cache_root>/compile — i.e. it sits with the dataset caches and follows a custom cache_root. Must be ext4 (255-char filenames); point it at an ext4 path if cache_root is on an encrypted/short-filename filesystem. Only used when compile_disk_cache is active.
compile:compile_cache_dir.label: Compile cache dir

compile:compile_disk_cache.description: 'auto' (default) persists Inductor/Triton kernels only when compile_dynamic is off (static shapes — where the cache actually hits; dynamic shapes are a no-op). Needs an ext4 cache dir; auto-disables with a warning on encrypted homes.
compile:compile_disk_cache.help: Values: 'auto' (default — enable only when compile is on AND compile_dynamic is off, where it actually helps), true (always on; warns if dynamic, since it won't help), false (never). Sets the Inductor/Triton on-disk caches so a second run with the SAME static shapes reuses the compiled kernels instead of recompiling (~30s of compile saved per run). With compile_dynamic on it is a no-op (dynamic-shape guards never match). The cache must live on an ext4-style filesystem (255-char filenames); on an encrypted home (~143-char limit) it auto-disables with a warning — set compile_cache_dir to an ext4 path. Only applies when compile is on.
compile:compile_disk_cache.label: Persist compile cache to disk

compile:compile_dynamic.description: Pass dynamic=True to torch.compile when input shapes vary between steps.
compile:compile_dynamic.help: Maps to torch.compile(dynamic=True). Leave off for fixed-shape training; turn on if input shapes change between steps so Inductor avoids recompiling per shape. Only applies when compile is on. Note: dynamic shapes defeat the on-disk compile cache (compile_disk_cache) — the cache only helps with fixed (static) shapes.
compile:compile_dynamic.label: torch.compile dynamic shapes

compile:compile_mode.description: Inductor mode passed to torch.compile. 'reduce-overhead' uses CUDA graphs to cut per-step launch overhead (best for fixed-shape steps). Leave unset for 'default'.
compile:compile_mode.help: Maps to torch.compile(mode=...). Options: 'default'; 'reduce-overhead' (CUDA-graph based, lowest per-step launch overhead — best for fixed-shape steps, costs a little extra VRAM for graph pools and can further reduce step time over default; benchmark per setup); 'max-autotune' and 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' (longer autotuning warmup). Only applies when compile is on.
compile:compile_mode.label: torch.compile mode

compile:compile_scope.description: 'model' (default) compiles the whole pipeline; 'block' compiles each transformer block alone so activation checkpointing and block swap stay eager. Required for the fp8 tensorwise speedup; measured 1.14x alone on krea2 bf16.
compile:compile_scope.help: 'block' compiles each transformer block on its own and leaves the layer loop (activation checkpointing, block-swap hooks, tuple plumbing) eager — whole-module compile measured ~0% on a swapped krea2 base because the trace graph-breaks on all of that. Block scope measured 1.14x alone (bf16) and is required to see the fp8 tensorwise GEMM speedup (model.transformer_fp8_matmul); only applies when compile is on.
compile:compile_scope.label: torch.compile scope

dataloader:dataloader_num_workers.description: Subprocess workers that load batches in parallel during training.
dataloader:dataloader_num_workers.help: 0 (default) loads in the main process, with dataloader_prefetch (on by default) overlapping the load with compute. Raise to 2–4 on Linux only if prefetch alone leaves the GPU idle waiting for batches (>0 is problematic on Windows/macOS).
dataloader:dataloader_num_workers.label: Train DataLoader workers

dataloader:dataloader_persistent_workers.description: Keep DataLoader worker processes alive between epochs instead of restarting them (default on).
dataloader:dataloader_persistent_workers.help: Turn off only if you see stale worker state or memory leaks across epoch boundaries.
dataloader:dataloader_persistent_workers.label: Persistent DataLoader workers

dataloader:dataloader_pin_memory.description: Allocate CPU batch tensors in page-locked memory for faster host-to-GPU copies.
dataloader:dataloader_pin_memory.help: Helps on Linux with dataloader_num_workers > 0; has little effect with the default prefetch thread. Off by default.
dataloader:dataloader_pin_memory.label: Pin memory (CUDA)

dataloader:dataloader_prefetch.description: Background thread that preloads the next batch while the current step trains.
dataloader:dataloader_prefetch.help: On by default: it overlaps loading the next batch (the next step's data, not the whole epoch) with the current step's compute. Only applies when dataloader_num_workers = 0. Off, the load runs synchronously on the main thread and stalls the GPU every step (measured ~67 ms/step). Same data either way.
dataloader:dataloader_prefetch.label: Prefetch next batch (thread)

dataloader:dataloader_prefetch_factor.description: Batches each DataLoader worker prefetches ahead (default 2, applies only when num_workers > 0).
dataloader:dataloader_prefetch_factor.help: Raise if workers are fast but the GPU still stalls waiting for batches. Lower if RAM is tight.
dataloader:dataloader_prefetch_factor.label: DataLoader prefetch factor

deepspeed:partition_method.description: How model layers are split across pipeline-parallel stages.
deepspeed:partition_method.help: Only matters with pipeline_stages > 1 (pipeline parallelism across multiple GPUs); ignored on a single stage / single GPU. parameters (default): balance VRAM by giving each stage a similar parameter count. uniform: same number of layers per stage. manual: set the exact split points yourself in partition_split. For one GPU, leave it alone — use blocks_to_swap + activation checkpointing to save VRAM instead.
deepspeed:partition_method.label: Partition method

deepspeed:partition_split.help: Only used with pipeline_stages > 1 and partition_method = manual. JSON list of layer indices where each stage ends (e.g. [10, 20] for 3 stages).
deepspeed:partition_split.label: Partition split (manual)

deepspeed:pipeline_stages.description: DeepSpeed pipeline parallel stages — set to the number of GPUs when using pipeline parallelism.
deepspeed:pipeline_stages.help: Default 1 (single GPU or tensor-parallel). Raise only when splitting the model across multiple GPUs; blocks_to_swap is the VRAM lever for single-GPU runs.
deepspeed:pipeline_stages.label: Pipeline stages

eval:disable_block_swap_for_eval.description: Load the full backbone onto GPU for eval passes even when blocks_to_swap is on.
eval:disable_block_swap_for_eval.help: Gives more accurate eval loss at the cost of temporarily using full-model VRAM. Enable if eval results look wrong with block swap active.
eval:disable_block_swap_for_eval.label: Disable block swap for eval

eval:eval_before_first_step.description: Run one eval pass before the first training step.
eval:eval_before_first_step.help: Useful for a loss baseline on validation data.
eval:eval_before_first_step.label: Eval before first step

eval:eval_datasets.description: List of paths or [{name, config}] tables.
eval:eval_datasets.help: Each entry is a path to a dataset TOML, or a table with name and config keys. Set at least one to enable the generalization probe — without it, val_gap_enable is a no-op.
eval:eval_datasets.label: Eval datasets

eval:eval_every_n_epochs.description: Run a validation pass at the end of every N epochs.
eval:eval_every_n_epochs.help: Simpler alternative to eval_every_n_steps when your dataset has a well-defined epoch boundary.
eval:eval_every_n_epochs.label: Eval every N epochs

eval:eval_every_n_examples.description: Run a validation pass every N training examples (converted to steps using global batch size).
eval:eval_every_n_examples.help: Run a validation pass every N training examples (converted to steps using global batch size).
eval:eval_every_n_examples.label: Eval every N examples

eval:eval_every_n_steps.description: Run a validation pass every N optimizer steps.
eval:eval_every_n_steps.help: Use this for fine-grained overfitting tracking; combine with val_gap_enable to log val/loss and val/gap.
eval:eval_every_n_steps.label: Eval every N steps

eval:eval_gradient_accumulation_steps.help: Raise to match training accumulation if your eval loss differs unexpectedly from train loss.
eval:eval_gradient_accumulation_steps.label: Eval grad accum

eval:val_gap_enable.description: Deterministic held-out val loss + train-val gap (overfitting signal). Uses the first eval dataset; no-ops if none.
eval:val_gap_enable.help: Forward-only probe on the existing eval cadence. The val curve uses the first eval dataset; a matched probe runs on a fixed train subset. Logs val/loss, train/probe and val/gap (val − train). No-ops if no eval dataset is configured.
eval:val_gap_enable.label: Train-val gap probe

eval:val_gap_probe_batches.description: Forward batches per probe (per timestep quantile). Smaller = faster.
eval:val_gap_probe_batches.help: Each probe runs this many forward-only batches per quantile to estimate val/loss and train/probe. Lower if the probe adds noticeable time to your eval cadence; raise for smoother, less noisy gap curves.
eval:val_gap_probe_batches.label: Gap probe batches

general:dataset.description: One or more dataset TOMLs (library ref or file path). Multiple entries are merged at train time (all [[directory]] blocks).
general:dataset.help: Each entry is a library ref (rengu-flow-dataset:<id> or rengu-flow-dataset:<id>:label) or a .toml path. The optional label after the id is only for reading the TOML; training resolves by id. Multiple entries merge all [[directory]] tables.
general:dataset.label: Dataset

general:engine.description: Training backend for this run. Precedence: the RENGU_ENGINE environment variable wins if set, then this field, then the host's platform default. Leave empty unless you need to force a specific backend (e.g. deepspeed for multi-GPU pipeline parallelism).
general:engine.help: Precedence: the RENGU_ENGINE environment variable wins if set, then this field, then the host's platform default. deepspeed adds multi-GPU pipeline parallelism, gradient_release, and the pipeline_stages/partition_method knobs; accelerate is the single-GPU path and raises if a deepspeed-only option (marked accordingly in the form) is set.
general:engine.label: Training engine

general:output_dir.help: Each run creates a dated folder under this path with checkpoints, logs, and copied config.
general:output_dir.label: Output directory

general:resume_from_checkpoint.description: Resume weights/optimizer from a prior run (trainer flag).
general:resume_from_checkpoint.help: Distinct from the UI “Resume folder” on jobs, which passes --resume_from_checkpoint with a run path.
general:resume_from_checkpoint.label: Resume from checkpoint

general:run_name.description: Optional suffix for timestamped run folder.
general:run_name.help: Appended to the timestamp so you can recognize experiments in output_dir.
general:run_name.label: Run name

logging_debug:logging_steps.description: Write train/loss and other scalars to TensorBoard every N optimizer steps.
logging_debug:logging_steps.help: Lower for finer loss curves; raise to reduce log file growth on very long runs.
logging_debug:logging_steps.label: Logging steps

logging_debug:min_image_exposure.description: Target average per-image exposure shown against the resolution-schedule exposure report printed at run startup — a reporting threshold only, it does not change training. Set it to the exposure you're aiming for to see how far each resolution/stage is from it.
logging_debug:min_image_exposure.help: Printed once at run startup alongside the estimated per-resolution image exposure. Setting a target only changes what the report compares against — it never changes training. Leave empty to print the estimate without a target line.
logging_debug:min_image_exposure.label: Target image exposure (report only)
logging_debug:min_image_exposure.placeholder: empty = no target in the report

logging_debug:steps_per_print.description: DeepSpeed prints step timing to the console every N steps.
logging_debug:steps_per_print.help: Lower for more frequent stdout feedback; raise to reduce log noise on long runs. Does not affect TensorBoard logging (use logging_steps for that).
logging_debug:steps_per_print.label: DeepSpeed steps_per_print

logging_debug:synthetic_num_batches.description: Use in-memory synthetic data for N batches (debug).
logging_debug:synthetic_num_batches.help: Skips real dataset cache; dataset TOML is not used for training data.
logging_debug:synthetic_num_batches.label: Synthetic batches (debug)

logging_debug:x_axis_examples.description: Plot TensorBoard/WandB x-axis as total examples seen instead of optimizer steps.
logging_debug:x_axis_examples.help: Useful when comparing runs with different batch sizes or gradient accumulation — example count normalizes the x-axis across them.
logging_debug:x_axis_examples.label: TensorBoard x-axis = examples

loss:huber_delta.description: Loss switch: when set, per-element loss is Huber(delta) instead of MSE. Presence-keyed and takes priority over smooth_l1_beta / pseudo_huber_c if more than one is set — only one loss is ever active.
loss:huber_delta.help: Presence-keyed: setting this key at all switches the per-element loss from MSE to F.huber_loss(delta=...). Takes priority over smooth_l1_beta and pseudo_huber_c if more than one is set — only one loss function is ever active.
loss:huber_delta.label: Huber loss delta

loss:pseudo_huber_c.description: Loss switch: when set (and huber_delta / smooth_l1_beta are not), per-element loss is sqrt((output-target)^2 + c^2) - c instead of MSE. Presence-keyed; lowest priority of the three.
loss:pseudo_huber_c.help: Presence-keyed: setting this key switches the per-element loss to sqrt((output-target)^2 + c^2) - c, unless huber_delta or smooth_l1_beta is also set (both take priority). Lowest priority of the three loss switches.
loss:pseudo_huber_c.label: Pseudo-Huber loss c

loss:smooth_l1_beta.description: Loss switch: when set (and huber_delta is not), per-element loss is Smooth-L1(beta) instead of MSE. Presence-keyed; mutually exclusive with huber_delta and pseudo_huber_c.
loss:smooth_l1_beta.help: Presence-keyed: setting this key switches the per-element loss to F.smooth_l1_loss(beta=...), unless huber_delta is also set (which wins). Mutually exclusive in practice with huber_delta and pseudo_huber_c.
loss:smooth_l1_beta.label: Smooth-L1 loss beta

memory:activation_budget_backoff.description: Only acts when activation_checkpointing='auto' AND compile=true: on a CUDA OOM, activation_memory_budget is lowered and the step retried instead of crashing the run (the configured budget is a ceiling, not a promise). Turn off to fail fast on OOM instead of silently settling for a lower budget.
memory:activation_budget_backoff.help: Only acts when activation_checkpointing='auto' AND compile=true — activation_memory_budget is a fraction the compile partitioner may overshoot on a new model/resolution/batch combination. On by default so an OOM backs off the budget and recompiles rather than ending the run; turn off to fail fast on OOM and see the real budget you configured.
memory:activation_budget_backoff.label: Auto-AC budget backoff on OOM

memory:activation_checkpoint_interval.description: Checkpoint every N transformer blocks (1 = every block). Measured neutral on Cosmos.
memory:activation_checkpoint_interval.help: Only applies when activation_checkpointing is on. 1 (default) checkpoints every block (most VRAM-saving, most recompute); higher keeps more activations to recompute less. Measured neutral on Cosmos at 1024 — leave at 1 unless you have a specific reason.
memory:activation_checkpoint_interval.label: Checkpoint interval (blocks)

memory:activation_checkpointing.description: true = full (lowest VRAM, safe default); false = fastest but OOMs at high res; 'auto' = compile's memory-budget partitioner (needs compile=true) — continuous VRAM/speed dial via activation_memory_budget, faster AND lighter than the retired 'selective' mode.
memory:activation_checkpointing.help: During the forward pass the intermediate activations are dropped and re-computed during backprop — large activation-memory savings for a small extra compute cost (an extra forward per checkpointed block). Keep it true on small GPUs; false can OOM. Values: true (full, lowest VRAM, safe default), false (fastest, highest VRAM — OOMs at high res), or 'auto' (compile's memory-budget partitioner picks the optimal save/recompute split per graph — requires compile=true; tune with activation_memory_budget; exact recompute, no precision cost). The old 'selective' (SAC) and 'unsloth' modes were retired: 'auto' beats SAC on both speed and VRAM; legacy configs fall back to true with a warning.
memory:activation_checkpointing.label: Activation checkpointing

memory:activation_memory_budget.description: Only for activation_checkpointing='auto'. 0.0 ~ full-checkpoint VRAM, 1.0 ~ no-checkpoint speed (plateaus ~0.5). Measured @1024 LoKr: 0.1 = -9.5% step time / 6.4 GB (beats SAC on both), 0.3 = -16% / 9.0 GB, 0.5 = -21% / 11.3 GB.
memory:activation_memory_budget.help: Fraction of activation memory the compile partitioner may keep instead of recomputing: 0.0 ~ full-checkpoint VRAM, 1.0 ~ no-checkpoint speed; gains plateau around 0.5. One global value for every resolution/shape in both compile modes. Recompute is exact (same math, no precision cost). Measured on Cosmos LoKr @1024 (RTX 4080, vs full checkpointing at 0.97 s / 5.8 GB): 0.1 = -9.5% step time / 6.4 GB, 0.3 = -16% / 9.0 GB (default), 0.5 = -21% / 11.3 GB. Requires compile = true. If a step OOMs, the budget backs off and recompiles instead of crashing (activation_budget_backoff, default on); the settled value is logged.
memory:activation_memory_budget.label: Auto-AC memory budget

memory:activation_offload.description: Stream saved activations to pinned CPU RAM (overlapped on side streams) instead of recomputing them — trades activation VRAM for PCIe bandwidth, not recompute FLOPs. Pairs with a raised activation_memory_budget. Costs host RAM; incompatible with compile_mode='reduce-overhead' (CUDA graphs).
memory:activation_offload.help: Activation checkpointing frees activation VRAM by DROPPING activations and RECOMPUTING them in the backward (costs extra forward FLOPs). Activation offload instead keeps the saved activations but moves them off the GPU: each large contiguous saved tensor is copied to a pinned CPU buffer on a side stream during the forward and streamed back, prefetched in reverse, during the backward — both directions overlap compute, so the cost is PCIe bandwidth, not recompute. Composes with activation_memory_budget (it is the reason you can RAISE the budget: the budget picks save-vs-recompute, the offloader decides where the saved ones live). Costs host RAM (the pinned buffers, can't page out). Payoff scales with activation size — high resolution / large batch / full fine-tune — and is negligible for small activations (low-res LoRA). NOT compatible with compile_mode='reduce-overhead' (CUDA-graph capture cannot record the side-stream copies).
memory:activation_offload.label: Activation offload

memory:activation_offload_max_ram_gb.description: Cap on pinned host RAM used for offloaded activations. Empty = no cap. Once the cap is hit, further activations stay in VRAM (so VRAM savings taper instead of exhausting host RAM).
memory:activation_offload_max_ram_gb.help: Pinned (page-locked) host RAM can't be paged out, so offloading a lot of activations can pressure system memory. This caps how much pinned RAM the offloader will use; once hit, further activations stay in VRAM (VRAM savings taper instead of exhausting host RAM). Leave empty for no cap when you have RAM to spare.
memory:activation_offload_max_ram_gb.label: Offload max host RAM (GB)

memory:activation_offload_min_tensor_mb.description: Only saved activations at least this large are offloaded; smaller tensors stay in VRAM (the per-tensor copy overhead isn't worth it). Lower it to offload more (useful when many medium activations add up); raise it to offload only the big ones.
memory:activation_offload_min_tensor_mb.help: Offloading a tensor costs a fixed D2H/H2D round trip, so tiny activations aren't worth moving — only saved activations at least this large go to pinned CPU. Lower it to offload more (when many medium-sized activations add up to real VRAM, e.g. higher resolution); raise it to move only the largest tensors and keep the rest resident. At low resolution most activations fall under the default, which is why offload barely engages there.
memory:activation_offload_min_tensor_mb.label: Offload min tensor size (MB)

memory:activation_offload_prefetch_mb.description: How many MB of offloaded activations to stream back to the GPU ahead of where the backward is running, to hide the H2D latency. Larger = more overlap but more transient VRAM for the in-flight tensors.
memory:activation_offload_prefetch_mb.help: During the backward the offloaded activations are copied back from CPU in reverse order, prefetched ahead of where the backward is running so the H2D latency hides behind compute. This sets how far ahead (in MB) to prefetch. Larger = more overlap but more transient VRAM for the in-flight tensors; smaller = less VRAM but the backward may stall waiting on copies.
memory:activation_offload_prefetch_mb.label: Offload backward prefetch (MB)

memory:block_swap_prefetch.description: Speed up block-swap transfers: pinned-DMA copies always, plus compute overlap when VRAM allows.
memory:block_swap_prefetch.help:
One switch, two effects (the offloader applies whichever fits — you don't tune them separately):
• Pinning (always, on CUDA): page-locks the swapped weights' CPU memory so each H2D copy runs as a full-bandwidth DMA instead of a ~half-speed pageable copy. This costs host RAM (the locked weights, a few GB), NOT VRAM, so it helps at ANY blocks_to_swap — including maximal swap, where it roughly halves step time on its own.
• Overlap (only when blocks_to_swap leaves ≥2 blocks resident): also prefetches the next block on a side stream while the current one computes. This keeps a second block resident, so it costs +1 block of VRAM and engages only when there is headroom for it.
Works for both adapter (LoRA/LoKr — streams only the frozen base weights, keeps the trainable adapters resident) and full-model (gradient_release) runs; loss is identical. Recommended ON whenever you block-swap and have spare host RAM. Turn it OFF if host RAM is tight (pinning can't page out), and note that on a nearly-full GPU the overlap's extra resident block can tip you into sysmem paging — measure the per-step cuda_peak_gb.
memory:block_swap_prefetch.label: Block-swap prefetch (overlap)

memory:block_swap_reclaim_every.description: Steps between empty_cache() calls while block swap is active (default 10).
memory:block_swap_reclaim_every.help: The single-buffered swap path allocates many shape-varying tensors per step, fragmenting the reserved pool by hundreds of MB between reclaims; a 50-step cadence let it grow 0.3-0.8 GB. Set 0 to disable, or raise it if the reclaim itself shows up in your step time. Lower it if a tight blocks_to_swap OOMs only after many steps.
memory:block_swap_reclaim_every.label: Block-swap cache reclaim interval

memory:blocks_to_swap.description: Stream UNet/DiT blocks between CPU and GPU so only a few stay resident.
memory:blocks_to_swap.help: SDXL, Cosmos Predict2, Krea 2 and Qwen-Image 2.1; requires pipeline_stages = 1. Works for both adapter and full-model training: adapters keep their small trainable params resident, while full-model (no [adapter]) additionally requires optimizer.gradient_release so the per-parameter step runs while the block is on the GPU. On ~8 GB cards this is the lever that makes a full SDXL fine-tune fit (e.g. blocks_to_swap = 6 → ~4.3 GB). Combine with activation_checkpointing. With gradient_release set, the Block-swap prefetch toggle appears. Qwen-Image 2.1 on 8 GB: blocks_to_swap = 24 with the fp8 base (transformer_fp8_matmul). See the low-VRAM recipe in the doc.
memory:blocks_to_swap.label: Blocks to swap

memory:reentrant_activation_checkpointin.description: Which PyTorch activation-checkpoint backend to use (reentrant vs non-reentrant).
memory:reentrant_activation_checkpointin.help: Only applies when activation_checkpointing is true. PyTorch has two checkpoint backends: reentrant (legacy, re-enters autograd) and non-reentrant (default, saved-tensor hooks). It defaults to true automatically in two cases: a 4-bit base with blocks_to_swap (reentrant lets swap eviction actually free blocks) and model.transformer_fp8_matmul + compile = true + compile_scope = "block" (non-reentrant recompute fails on the compiled block). Otherwise leave it unset.
memory:reentrant_activation_checkpointin.label: Reentrant checkpointing

model:model.diffusers_path.description: The whole Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 diffusers download (transformer/, vae/, text_encoder/, processor/); fills any of the three file fields above left empty. Set either this or the three files.
model:model.diffusers_path.help: Optional. Point at the folder holding transformer/, vae/, text_encoder/ and processor/ (e.g. the Hugging Face cache snapshot) and leave the file fields empty — each resolves to <folder>/<subfolder>; files you set explicitly always win. Never a repo id; nothing is downloaded.
model:model.diffusers_path.label: Diffusers folder (alternative)

model:model.dtype.description: Default precision for VAE, text stack, adapters, and most weights.
model:model.dtype.help: Common: bfloat16, float16. Cosmos: VAE, text encoder (Qwen3/T5) and sensitive DiT parts (embedders, norms, 1D params). Bulk DiT weights use this too unless transformer_dtype is set. SDXL: UNet and encoders. Adapter weights do not follow it: they default to float32 (adapter.dtype).
model:model.dtype.label: Model dtype

model:model.fp8_grad_mode.description: Input-gradient GEMM precision through the frozen fp8 base, only used when transformer_fp8_matmul is on: fp8 is faster, bf16 (default) keeps the clean gradient.
model:model.fp8_grad_mode.help: 'bf16' (default) keeps the backward's input-gradient GEMM unquantized; 'fp8' runs it through the same e4m3 tensorwise kernel as the forward (faster). Only takes effect when model.transformer_fp8_matmul is true.
model:model.fp8_grad_mode.label: fp8 backward gradient precision

model:model.processor_path.description: Folder with the tokenizer files; defaults to <diffusers folder>/processor, else the bundled Qwen3-VL tokenizer.
model:model.processor_path.help: Defaults to <diffusers_path>/processor, else the Qwen3-VL tokenizer and image processor bundled with rengu (identical tokenization of the Qwen-Image 2.1 prompt template).
model:model.processor_path.label: Processor / tokenizer override

model:model.shift.description: Fixed timestep shift (> 0), overriding the resolution-aware dynamic shift of the reference scheduler (exponential, mu 0.5 at 256 latent tokens to 0.9 at 8192; 1024x1024 = 4096 tokens). Empty keeps the dynamic default.
model:model.shift.help: By default training timesteps follow the reference scheduler's exponential shift: mu interpolates from 0.5 at 256 latent tokens to 0.9 at 8192 (1024x1024 = 4096 tokens, mu ~0.70). A number here replaces it for every resolution.
model:model.shift.label: Fixed timestep shift

model:model.sigmoid_scale.description: Scale applied to the logit-normal sample before sigmoid, only used when timestep_sample_method is logit_normal.
model:model.sigmoid_scale.help: Only used with timestep_sample_method = logit_normal. Raising it pushes sampled timesteps toward the extremes (near 0 or 1).
model:model.sigmoid_scale.label: Logit-normal sigmoid scale

model:model.text_encoder_offload.description: How the 17.5 GB Qwen3-VL-8B encoder runs while captions are cached: auto (default) streams its 36 decoder layers from pinned host RAM when it does not fit in free VRAM, stream always does, none loads it whole onto the GPU.
model:model.text_encoder_offload.help: auto (default): stream the 36 decoder layers one at a time from pinned host RAM when the encoder does not fit in free VRAM (~2 GB VRAM, ~16 GB host RAM); stream: always; none: load it whole onto the GPU (needs ~20 GB free). The encoder loads only when captions still need encoding and is unloaded after caching.
model:model.text_encoder_offload.label: Text encoder placement

model:model.text_encoder_path.description: ComfyUI's qwen3vl_8b_bf16.safetensors (or the transformers text_encoder/ folder); includes the vision tower edit training needs. Optional when the diffusers folder below is set.
model:model.text_encoder_path.help: ComfyUI's qwen3vl_8b_bf16.safetensors or the diffusers text_encoder/ folder; both carry the vision tower that edit training (control_path) uses. Captions are encoded once into the cache; int8 / w4a8 files are refused.
model:model.text_encoder_path.label: Text encoder — Qwen3-VL-8B (.safetensors)

model:model.timestep_sample_method.description: How training timesteps are sampled per step: logit_normal (default) or uniform.
model:model.timestep_sample_method.help: logit_normal concentrates steps on mid-range noise levels; uniform samples t evenly in [0, 1]. The resolution-aware shift (or model.shift) is applied on top of either.
model:model.timestep_sample_method.label: Timestep sample method

model:model.transformer_4bit.description: Stores the frozen DiT block linears as 4-bit NF4 (~4 GB instead of ~14 GB bf16); the adapter trains on top at full precision. Pair with adapter type LoKr (LyCORIS kinds refuse a quantized base).
model:model.transformer_4bit.help: Adapter training only — the quantized base stays frozen while the adapter trains in full precision on top. The 7B DiT drops from ~14 GB bf16 to ~4 GB. Mutually exclusive with model.transformer_fp8_matmul. Use adapter type LoKr: the LyCORIS kinds reject a quantized base.
model:model.transformer_4bit.label: Quantize base to 4-bit (NF4)

model:model.transformer_dtype.description: DiT checkpoint load only; defaults to Model dtype. VAE/text unchanged.
model:model.transformer_dtype.help: The VAE, the Qwen3-VL text encoder and the adapters keep model.dtype. Leave empty unless you need a different DiT load precision.
model:model.transformer_dtype.label: Main model load dtype

model:model.transformer_fp8_matmul.description: Tensorwise-scaled e4m3 quantization of the frozen DiT's block linears (mutually exclusive with transformer_4bit): the base drops from ~14.2 to ~7.3 GB. Needs an sm89+ GPU (RTX 40xx / Ada); pair with blocks_to_swap on 8-16 GB cards.
model:model.transformer_fp8_matmul.help: Adapter training only. The 7B DiT drops from ~14.2 GB to ~7.3 GB. Needs an sm89+ GPU (RTX 40xx / Ada); on older cards use transformer_4bit with LoKr instead. Mutually exclusive with model.transformer_4bit. The 8 GB recipe pairs it with blocks_to_swap = 24 and activation checkpointing.
model:model.transformer_fp8_matmul.label: Quantize base to fp8 (tensorwise scaled matmul)

model:model.transformer_path.description: The 14 GB DiT you train: ComfyUI's qwen_image_2.1_bf16.safetensors (a diffusers transformer/ folder also works). Optional when the diffusers folder below is set.
model:model.transformer_path.help: ComfyUI's qwen_image_2.1_bf16.safetensors (its fused img_mlp.gate_up is split on load), a diffusers-layout file or the diffusers transformer/ folder. Pre-quantized int8_convrot / fp8 files cannot be trained; use the bf16 file.
model:model.transformer_path.label: Main model (.safetensors)

model:model.type.help: Selects which model code loads (e.g. sdxl, cosmos_predict2, krea2, qwen_image21).
model:model.type.label: Model type

model:model.vae_path.description: Qwen-Image 2.1's own RGBA VAE: ComfyUI's qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors (or the diffusers vae/ folder). Optional when the diffusers folder below is set.
model:model.vae_path.help: ComfyUI's qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors (original layout, converted on load), a diffusers-layout file or the diffusers vae/ folder. Training reads your images through it to build the latent cache.
model:model.vae_path.label: Image VAE (.safetensors)

oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.bump_block_s.description: On reaching 'max OOMs in window', swap more transformer blocks to CPU (freeing base-model VRAM) and keep training instead of aborting — repeats up to every block swapped, then saves and stops. Only helps if blocks_to_swap started below the max.
oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.bump_block_s.help: On reaching 'max OOMs in window', swap more transformer blocks to CPU (freeing base-model VRAM) and keep training instead of aborting — repeats up to every block swapped, then saves and stops. Only helps if blocks_to_swap started below the max.
oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.bump_block_s.label: Raise block swap on repeated OOM

oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.clear_cache_.description: Run empty_cache() + ipc_collect() on each OOM skip to release the fragmented reserved pool before retrying the next step.
oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.clear_cache_.help: Run empty_cache() + ipc_collect() on each OOM skip to release the fragmented reserved pool before retrying the next step.
oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.clear_cache_.label: Empty CUDA cache on skip

oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.enabled.description: Catch a CUDA OOM during a training step, free the CUDA cache, and skip that batch instead of crashing — recovers from transient fragmentation-driven OOMs. Once 'max OOMs in window' OOMs land within a 10-step window it saves an emergency checkpoint and stops.
oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.enabled.help: Catch a CUDA OOM during a training step, free the CUDA cache, and skip that batch instead of crashing — recovers from transient fragmentation-driven OOMs. Once 'max OOMs in window' OOMs land within a 10-step window it saves an emergency checkpoint and stops.
oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.enabled.label: Skip step on CUDA OOM

oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.max_in_windo.description: Act (bump block swap, or abort with an emergency checkpoint) once this many steps OOM within any 10-step window — catches OOMs interleaved with good steps, not just back-to-back ones.
oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.max_in_windo.help: Act (bump block swap, or abort with an emergency checkpoint) once this many steps OOM within any 10-step window — catches OOMs interleaved with good steps, not just back-to-back ones.
oom_recovery:train.oom_skip.max_in_windo.label: Max OOMs in a 10-step window

optimizer:optimizer.extra_params.description: All [optimizer] keys (lr, betas, weight_decay, gradient_release, …). Pre-filled when you change optimizer type; see docs for per-type tables.
optimizer:optimizer.extra_params.help: Key-value rows merged into [optimizer] in TOML. Built-in registry names are pre-filled when you change optimizer type (lr, betas, type-specific keys). Custom class paths start empty until you add rows. See the user guide for per-optimizer parameter tables and links to PyTorch, bitsandbytes, and Prodigy docs.
optimizer:optimizer.extra_params.label: Optimizer parameters

optimizer:optimizer.gradient_release.description: Runs each parameter's optimizer step inside the backward pass instead of after gradient accumulation — required for full-model block swap (a block's optimizer step must run while it is still resident on GPU). DeepSpeed engine only; accelerate raises at train time. Needs pipeline_stages = 1.
optimizer:optimizer.gradient_release.help: Instead of accumulating gradients and stepping the optimizer once per micro-batch group, each parameter's optimizer.step() runs as soon as its gradient is ready, then the gradient is freed immediately. Required for full-model training with blocks_to_swap (a swapped block's optimizer step must happen while it is still on GPU) — without it, a full finetune has to keep the whole optimizer state resident. Patches the DeepSpeed pipeline engine, so it requires engine='deepspeed' (accelerate raises at train time) and pipeline_stages = 1 / data-parallel world size 1.
optimizer:optimizer.gradient_release.label: Gradient release

optimizer:optimizer.type.description: Built-in registry names, pytorch_optimizer classes, or module.Class path.
optimizer:optimizer.type.help: Suggestions list common registry names. Type a custom class name if needed; required packages are installed automatically when training starts.
optimizer:optimizer.type.label: Optimizer type

preview:disable_block_swap_for_preview.description: Load the full backbone onto GPU for preview sampling even when blocks_to_swap is on.
preview:disable_block_swap_for_preview.help: Faster previews at the cost of temporarily using full-model VRAM. Enable if preview quality looks degraded with block swap active.
preview:disable_block_swap_for_preview.label: Disable block swap for preview

preview:preview.control_resolution.description: Side of the target area of edit-preview condition images (Qwen-Image 2.1).
preview:preview.control_resolution.help: Only used by preview prompts with control_images: each condition image keeps its aspect and is resized to an area of control_resolution² (floored to 32 px), like training control images. Empty uses the side of the preview width × height (1024 by default). At least 256 (the vision encoder's minimum area).
preview:preview.control_resolution.label: Edit preview condition resolution

preview:preview.enabled.description: Off by default — generating samples during training adds significant VRAM and time (a 1024×1024 SDXL preview can OOM on small GPUs). Enable it explicitly when you want in-training samples.
preview:preview.enabled.help: Images are written to the run preview/ folder and shown in TensorBoard. Enable to visually track quality without stopping the run.
preview:preview.enabled.label: Enabled

preview:preview.guidance_scale.description: CFG scale for previews; Qwen-Image 2.1 samples without CFG (default 1.0).
preview:preview.guidance_scale.help: 1.0 runs one conditional pass per step, like the reference. Above 1.0 CFG runs with the negative prompt (an empty one is encoded as a single space) as neg + g*(pos - neg), doubling the preview cost.
preview:preview.guidance_scale.label: Guidance scale

preview:preview.height.help: Set to a resolution your model supports; mismatch with the trained resolution can make previews look blurry or distorted.
preview:preview.height.label: Height

preview:preview.negative_prompt.description: Negative prompt applied to every preview image (SDXL).
preview:preview.negative_prompt.help: Shared across all preview prompts. Leave empty for Cosmos/Anima, which does not use a negative prompt during sampling.
preview:preview.negative_prompt.label: Negative prompt

preview:preview.num_inference_steps.description: Denoising steps per preview image (Qwen-Image 2.1 default 28).
preview:preview.num_inference_steps.help: Euler steps over the reference sigma schedule (resolution-aware shift, last step at 0.02). The reference sampler uses 40; 28 keeps previews faster.
preview:preview.num_inference_steps.label: Inference steps

preview:preview.preview_before_first_ste.description: Run one preview pass before step 1 to capture the untrained baseline.
preview:preview.preview_before_first_ste.help: Useful for visually comparing the model's output before and after training begins.
preview:preview.preview_before_first_ste.label: Preview before first step

preview:preview.preview_blocks_to_swap.description: Number of DiT blocks to keep on CPU during preview sampling (Cosmos, Krea 2, Qwen-Image 2.1).
preview:preview.preview_blocks_to_swap.help: Reduces preview VRAM at the cost of slower sampling. Raise if preview sampling OOMs after enabling preview_offload_text_encoder. Qwen-Image 2.1 on 8 GB cards: 32 (all blocks).
preview:preview.preview_blocks_to_swap.label: Preview blocks to swap

preview:preview.preview_every_n_epochs.description: Generate preview images at the end of every N epochs.
preview:preview.preview_every_n_epochs.help: Alternative to preview_every_n_steps for epoch-based runs. Preview inference runs after the epoch save, so it does not delay checkpointing.
preview:preview.preview_every_n_epochs.label: Preview every N epochs

preview:preview.preview_every_n_steps.description: Generate preview images every N optimizer steps.
preview:preview.preview_every_n_steps.help: Lower values give more frequent quality checks at the cost of extra inference time per step. Combine with preview_before_first_step for a baseline.
preview:preview.preview_every_n_steps.label: Preview every N steps

preview:preview.preview_offload_text_enc.description: Move the text encoder to CPU during preview sampling to free VRAM (Cosmos, Krea 2, Qwen-Image 2.1).
preview:preview.preview_offload_text_enc.help: Enable if preview sampling OOMs; the transfer adds latency but lets the DiT use more VRAM during generation.
preview:preview.preview_offload_text_enc.label: Offload text encoder during preview

preview:preview.preview_save_png.description: Write preview images as PNG files under the run preview/ folder (on by default).
preview:preview.preview_save_png.help: Turn off only to suppress preview files on disk; images still appear in TensorBoard via the in-memory path.
preview:preview.preview_save_png.label: Save preview PNGs

preview:preview.prompts.description: Each entry becomes one item under preview.prompts in TOML.
preview:preview.prompts.help: Each entry becomes one item in preview.prompts — use the Add sampling button to manage the list.
preview:preview.prompts.label: Preview configurations

preview:preview.seed.description: Base RNG seed for preview images.
preview:preview.seed.help: Fixed seed produces consistent previews across steps so changes in quality are clearly visible. Change if the seed happens to pick an unrepresentative starting noise.
preview:preview.seed.label: Seed

preview:preview.seed_stride.description: Optional seed offset applied per training step.
preview:preview.seed_stride.help: The default 0 keeps each prompt's noise fixed across steps so previews show model evolution. Set a positive value only when you intentionally want different noise at every preview.
preview:preview.seed_stride.label: Seed stride

preview:preview.width.help: Set to a resolution your model supports; mismatch with the trained resolution can make previews look blurry or distorted.
preview:preview.width.label: Width

scheduler:lr_scheduler.description: Registry name (cosine, rex, linear, …) or fully-qualified scheduler class.
scheduler:lr_scheduler.help: Built-in names: constant, linear, cosine, rex, wsd, none. wsd = constant LR then a decay tail carved from the total (NOT added: a 1000-step run with decay 100 is 900 stable + 100 decay). Set decay: float=fraction of the run, int=absolute steps; decay_type rex/cosine/linear, rex_d, lr_min. With wsd the trainer auto-saves a protected 'predecay' fork checkpoint at the decay onset, so you can extend the run by resuming from it with a larger epochs/max_steps. For custom classes, use Scheduler parameters and runtime token string values (total_steps, effective_total_steps, …) — open the (i) help on that field for meanings; resolved when training starts.
scheduler:lr_scheduler.label: Scheduler type

scheduler:lr_scheduler_args.extra_params.description: Scheduler constructor kwargs (lr_min, total_iters, T_max, …) under [lr_scheduler_args].
scheduler:lr_scheduler_args.extra_params.help:
Key-value rows map to [lr_scheduler_args] (not top-level warmup_steps — use the Warmup steps field). Built-in names and PyTorch class paths are pre-filled when you change scheduler type.

Runtime tokens (string values → integers at train time):
• total_steps — Optimizer steps for the full run (epochs × steps_per_epoch), passed when the scheduler is resolved.
• effective_total_steps — min(total_steps, max_steps) when max_steps is a positive integer in config; otherwise total_steps.
• steps_per_epoch — Optimizer steps in one epoch after gradient accumulation, passed when the scheduler is resolved.
• epochs — epochs from config (default 1 if omitted).
• max_steps — max_steps from config when set to a positive integer; omitted from substitution otherwise.
• gradient_accumulation_steps — gradient_accumulation_steps from config when set; omitted from substitution otherwise.

scheduler:warmup_steps.description: Trainer-level linear LR warmup before the main scheduler (not a [lr_scheduler_args] constructor kwarg).
scheduler:warmup_steps.help: Top-level warmup_steps in TOML. When > 0 and lr_scheduler is not none, training wraps the resolved scheduler with a short LinearLR warmup phase — for built-in names and fully-qualified PyTorch classes alike. Not a [lr_scheduler_args] constructor kwarg; use [lr_scheduler_args] only if your class defines its own warmup under a different parameter name.
scheduler:warmup_steps.label: Warmup steps

te_cache:cache_keep_in_memory.description: Load resumed cache slices fully into RAM.
te_cache:cache_keep_in_memory.help: false saves RAM on large datasets; train reads still use OS page cache.
te_cache:cache_keep_in_memory.label: Keep HF slice in RAM during cache

te_cache:cache_num_proc.description: CPU processes for metadata map and latent/TE cache.
te_cache:cache_num_proc.help: Default caps at 8. Lower if RAM is tight during --cache_only.
te_cache:cache_num_proc.label: Cache CPU workers

te_cache:cache_root.description: Overrides where dataset latent/text-embedding caches (and the compile cache under it) are written. Point it at a larger/faster disk when caching many datasets or the default location runs low on space.
te_cache:cache_root.help: Empty uses <repo>/cache. A legacy cache_root left in the dataset TOML is only honored when this field is empty (deprecated path, logs a warning); when both are set, this field wins and the dataset TOML value is ignored.
te_cache:cache_root.label: Cache root directory

te_cache:caching_batch_size.description: Batch size for the dataset latent/text cache pass.
te_cache:caching_batch_size.help: Larger values can speed cache but use more VRAM during caching. For Qwen-Image 2.1 with a streamed text encoder, each encoding batch sends the whole encoder over PCIe once, so a larger batch encodes more captions per pass.
te_cache:caching_batch_size.label: Dataset cache batch size

tracking:tracking.enabled.description: Master switch for experiment tracking (run.json + TB + timeline).
tracking:tracking.enabled.help: When off, the run trains with a no-op sink and writes no tracking artifacts.
tracking:tracking.enabled.label: Enable tracking

tracking:tracking.system_sampler.enabled.description: Periodically sample GPU/CPU/RAM usage and log as system/* scalars.
tracking:tracking.system_sampler.enabled.help: Enable to see hardware utilisation alongside training loss in TensorBoard. Turn off if the sampler adds overhead on very fast steps.
tracking:tracking.system_sampler.enabled.label: Sample system metrics (GPU/CPU)

tracking:tracking.wandb.api_key.description: WandB API key (prefer WANDB_API_KEY env var).
tracking:tracking.wandb.api_key.help: WandB API key (prefer WANDB_API_KEY env var).
tracking:tracking.wandb.api_key.label: WandB API key

tracking:tracking.wandb.project.description: WandB project name — required when 'wandb' is in tracking.backends.
tracking:tracking.wandb.project.help: WandB project name — required when 'wandb' is in tracking.backends.
tracking:tracking.wandb.project.label: WandB project

tracking:tracking.wandb.run_name.description: Display name for this run in WandB.
tracking:tracking.wandb.run_name.help: Defaults to the run directory name if omitted.
tracking:tracking.wandb.run_name.label: WandB run name

training:ema_decay.description: Optional; fp32 CPU shadow weights. Applied at export and persisted across resume.
training:ema_decay.help: Float in (0, 1), e.g. 0.999; omit to disable. The shadow is swapped into the model at export and saved inside each resume checkpoint, so exported weights are the smoothed average rather than the last noisy step. Use when late-training samples swing in quality between neighbouring checkpoints.
training:ema_decay.label: EMA decay

training:ema_update_interval.description: Update the EMA shadow every N steps instead of every step (default 1).
training:ema_update_interval.help: The shadow lives on CPU, so each update costs a GPU->CPU copy of every trainable tensor on the critical path; decay is compounded by N so the effective averaging window is unchanged. Raise to 4-8 if enabling ema_decay visibly slowed your s/it.
training:ema_update_interval.label: EMA update interval

training:epochs.description: Passes over the full training dataset; each pass visits every image once.
training:epochs.help: One epoch = one complete pass over all images at each configured resolution. Raise if the model hasn't converged; lower if val/gap is rising (overfitting signal).
training:epochs.label: Epochs

training:gradient_accumulation_steps.description: Micro-steps to accumulate before optimizer step.
training:gradient_accumulation_steps.help: Increases effective batch without raising micro_batch VRAM, but each optimizer step does more work (e.g. 2× accum ≈ ~2× wall time per step in Anima smokes).
training:gradient_accumulation_steps.label: Gradient accumulation

training:gradient_clipping.description: Clips gradient norm to this value before the optimizer step (0 = off).
training:gradient_clipping.help: Prevents gradient spikes from destabilizing training. Lower if loss spikes suddenly mid-run; common values are 0.5–1.0.
training:gradient_clipping.label: Gradient clipping

training:image_micro_batch_size_per_gpu.description: Per-GPU micro-batch for image-only steps when mixing image+video; falls back to micro_batch_size_per_gpu. For an advanced per-modality dict, edit it in the TOML tab.
training:image_micro_batch_size_per_gpu.help: Integer or per-resolution map like micro_batch_size_per_gpu (e.g. 512 -> 2, 1024 -> 1); unset = image buckets use micro_batch_size_per_gpu. Set it when image steps leave the GPU under-filled at the batch size the video buckets need.
training:image_micro_batch_size_per_gpu.label: Image micro batch per GPU

training:max_steps.description: Optional cap; stops after N optimizer steps.
training:max_steps.label: Max steps

training:micro_batch_size_per_gpu.description: Uniform integer, or per-resolution (e.g. 512 -> 2, 1024 -> 1) to batch up low resolutions where the GPU is under-filled.
training:micro_batch_size_per_gpu.help: Per-resolution mode (e.g. 512 -> 2, 1024 -> 1) lets low resolutions batch up where the GPU is under-filled while the detail resolution stays at what fits: measured on a 16 GB 4080, batching pays at 512 (bs1->bs2 is -18% per sample) and nothing at 1024 (GEMM-saturated). Buckets pick the numerically closest configured resolution.
training:micro_batch_size_per_gpu.label: Micro batch per GPU

training:train_seed.description: RNG seed for training, tag dropout, and dataloader shuffle (default 42).
training:train_seed.help: Change to reproduce a run with a different random order, or to break a run that appears to be stuck in a bad local pattern.
training:train_seed.label: Training seed
